prompt: Literary translations should be drafted, critiqued for tone and accuracy by a second model, and revised until the critic has no major notes.
tells: critiqued for tone and accuracy by a second model
revised until the critic has no major notes
why: Generator and evaluator in a loop, refining a draft against clear criteria.
trap: A fixed chain runs once; this repeats until the evaluation passes.

prompt: Generated API docs must meet a 15-point style checklist. A checker model scores each draft against it and sends feedback for another pass.
why: Clear criteria make the evaluator's feedback actionable for the next draft.
trap: It loops, but over one draft and a fixed rubric rather than open-ended actions.

prompt: Generated SQL is run against a sample database; a reviewer model compares the results to the question and asks for a corrected query if they don't match.
tells: reviewer model compares the results to the question
why: Draft → evaluate → revise, with execution results feeding the evaluation.
trap: It runs a tool, but the pattern is the critique-and-revise loop.

prompt: Write a headline, have a second call rate it for clarity and accuracy, and rewrite it until it scores at least 8 out of 10.
tells: have a second call rate it
trap: Generating five and voting would be parallelization; this improves one draft.

prompt: A model writes a function, a reviewer model lists issues against the team's style guide, and the writer revises until the reviewer approves.
tells: writer revises until the reviewer approves
why: Generate, evaluate against criteria, revise: repeated until it passes.
trap: A single review pass would be a chain; the repeat-until-approved loop is the pattern.

prompt: A summarizer drafts, a checker flags any claim not supported by the source, and the summarizer rewrites until nothing is flagged.
tells: a checker flags any claim not supported
why: A clear criterion (supported by the source) lets the evaluator drive revisions.
trap: Generating several summaries and voting is parallelization, not refinement.

prompt: Draft a cover letter, score it against a rubric of clarity, specificity and tone, and keep revising until every score is at least 4 of 5.
why: Rubric-driven critique and revision in a loop.
trap: The steps repeat based on the score, so it isn't a fixed chain.

prompt: A critique-and-revise loop on marketing copy never settles: the critic's feedback is just "make it more engaging" every round.
why: Evaluator-optimizer only works with clear, checkable criteria; give the critic a concrete rubric.
trap: It's a loop that doesn't stop, but the fix is the evaluator's criteria, not a step budget.
